With advancing technology and ever-evolving needs, businesses are moving towards a more hybrid when it comes to cloud infrastructure. Hybrid cloud infrastructure allows businesses to enjoy the benefits of both private and public clouds. As per the needs of the business, it can go back and forth between the two and save considerable time and effort that can come up with the migration of data over different cloud infrastructures.

What is Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure?

Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure refers to a mixed environment that consists of mixed computing, storage, and services on the cloud premises that are both public and private. This type of infrastructure allows orchestration on more than one platform, making it an ideal choice for many organizations.

It allows the movement of workload from one cloud to another as per the needs of the organization. Hybrid cloud infrastructure allows organizations to keep their sensitive data on the private cloud and only share what they need to share on the public cloud. This type of infrastructure grants organizations a greater degree of flexibility and is also scalable. At the same time, it allows businesses to protect their data from potential threats.

Investing in a hybrid cloud environment allows organizations to leverage the benefits of both private and public clouds. The private cloud provides them with better control, security, and customization. On the other hand, the public cloud is more cost-effective and accessible. Additionally, it also allows greater scalability.

Common Use Cases for Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure

There are many cases in which hybrid cloud infrastructure can be used by organizations. It already provides businesses with dual benefits. However, they manifest in many ways. Below, we have provided the most common use cases for hybrid cloud infrastructure in detail.

Hybrid Cloud Backup

One of the biggest advantages of hybrid cloud infrastructure is that it provides backup. It provides organizations with a strong control over their data. It provides protection over data in case of any attacks or thefts. The backup infrastructure provided by hybrid cloud infrastructure is scalable and adaptable. In case of any threat or loss of data, hybrid cloud infrastructure provides a good backup.

Disaster Recovery

One of the most common case uses of hybrid cloud infrastructure is disaster recovery. As organizations have infrastructure backup on both private and public cloud infrastructure, it provides them with an easy transition in case of any unfortunate event. Whether it is a hardware breakdown or a full-fledged cyber attack, hybrid cloud infrastructure is considered one of the best choices for disaster recovery. Companies often create a backup infrastructure on the public cloud to recover from any disaster swiftly.

Cloud Bursting

Cloud burst refers to situations in which, temporarily, there is a hike in traffic. Hybrid cloud infrastructure allows you to deal with such bursts efficiently. Since it provides a low-latency network between public and private clouds that is also secured, it is a good way of ensuring that you are able to handle any unforeseen hike in traffic well.

Big Data Analytics

Nowadays, it is common for organizations to deal with large volumes of data. It can be hard and expensive for an organization to store it. With hybrid cloud infrastructure, it is easier to store larger volumes of data on the public cloud at relatively less cost. It also helps organizations store confidential data in a private cloud so that it stays protected.

Content Delivery

Hybrid clouds are also very efficient when it comes to content delivery. When organizations employ hybrid cloud infrastructure, they are able to share content with end users more effectively. Having a private cloud allows content to stay safe, whereas a public cloud is more scalable and cost-effective. Having the option to use either based on the nature of the content is an advantage provided by hybrid cloud infrastructure.

Testing Workloads

New organizations often face issues in calculating and managing their workloads. Having a hybrid cloud infrastructure will help you avoid any failures that can be caused by an untested workload. It will also help save costs for new organizations, and few things can be worse than investing in a technology that does not perform efficiently. The hybrid infrastructure allows one to test what works best for their particular workload and then shift to the infrastructure that provides the best results.

Software Development and Testing

Development, testing, and release of websites and apps are common functions that almost all organizations need to perform at one point or another. Development and testing can be done on the public cloud, whereas operational needs can be completed on a private cloud. It allows organizations to have greater control. It is cost-effective and also a rapid and efficient process.

Software Compatibility

It is easier for your organization to run an independent software vendor when you are working with a hybrid cloud infrastructure. It is easier to migrate software, and the deployment also becomes easier when you are working with a hybrid cloud infrastructure due to increased productivity and adaptability.

Extension of Data Centre

By using a cloud hybrid infrastructure, data can be collected in an organized and efficient manner. Especially in industries that are controlled by the government, as per the policy changes, cloud hybrid infrastructure enables organizations to move data with greater efficiency. It can also help deal with latency issues that arise from the end users.

Automation of IT Operations

Hybrid cloud infrastructure helps in automating IT operations. This is also known as self-service IT or cloud service brokering. This ensures that the users have the agility to meet the business objectives. It provides the end users with push-button features that help them deploy to the public and private cloud without any hassles. It provides end users with autonomy and reduces their reliance on the operations team.

When to Opt For Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure?

While there are many ways hybrid cloud infrastructure is useful, it is important to consider your needs before opting for it. A thorough research about the infrastructure, in addition to a deep assessment of your organization’s needs, is crucial. Consider these factors before choosing a hybrid cloud infrastructure.

Dynamic Workloads – If you have workloads that are constantly changing, then opting for a hybrid cloud infrastructure will be a good decision for your organization. You can use a public infrastructure for dynamic workload and store volatile content on a private cloud.

Big Data Processing – It is difficult to process the constant values of big data constantly at all times. Hybrid cloud infrastructure will allow you to run certain data processing on the public cloud and others on the private cloud based on your needs and the type of data.

Flexibility – You can assess your current cloud needs. However, there is no way to assess your future needs with accuracy. To be sure that you are ready to meet your future needs, opting for a hybrid cloud infrastructure is an ideal solution. As your business needs change, you will be able to switch from private cloud to public cloud or vice-versa seamlessly and without spending much money.

Separation of Workloads – If you want to store your information efficiently, then opt for a hybrid cloud infrastructure. You can store sensitive client data on the private cloud and other data on the public cloud to have an efficient workload distribution.

Pacing – When you are working with data, store some on the public cloud and other data on the private cloud. See what is working out best for you. Hybrid cloud infrastructure is the best option, considering you get to experience both and can move cloud at your own pace and convenience.

Capacity Needs – When it comes to projects, they can be short-term or long-term, and hybrid cloud infrastructure allows you to store data as per your needs. For short-term projects, companies can leverage the public cloud, which will help them save money. It is a good way of ensuring you invest mindfully in your projects.

To Sum Up

Cloud hybrid infrastructure is an excellent way for organizations to deal with complex problems. There are many use cases that enable an organization to leverage and benefit from this type of infrastructure. By integrating a hybrid cloud, organizations can experience the best of both worlds. They can use both private and public cloud infrastructure as per their needs. It will result in many benefits, such as saving costs, increasing scalability, and agility. Hybrid cloud infrastructures also improve efficiency and provide greater protection.
Suppose you are planning to integrate hybrid cloud infrastructure in your business operations. In that case, you should also assess your needs and choose based on what type of cloud storage is most needed by your organization.
